transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Partnerships), Sophie Lee (Neon Head of Partnerships), Carlos Mendez (Neon Sales Dir), Ibrahim Khan (Neon Solutions Architect), Ava Torres (Neon Biz Ops)

Summary (auto): Weekly co-sell pipeline review. Covered three high-priority deals, technical validation asks for two enterprise prospects, alignment on ownership and next steps to move one opportunity to demo stage. Action items assigned.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:07 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Yep, loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): Cool. Quick agenda — run through the pipeline, flag any at-risk deals, call out technical blockers, and agree owners for next actions. Owen will chime in on the perf/benchmark asks.
00:20 Speaker 3 (Owen): Hi all, will do. I added a short note in the sheet about the 8k context perf we talked about last week.
00:30 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Awesome. We have Carlos here — going to run through the list we sent earlier, highlight three we want to push.
00:38 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Also quick note, we had legal ask around data residency for one deal — might need Private deploy or VPC option.
00:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. We can map that to Redwood Private — we'll include the relevant security docs.
01:00 Speaker 3 (Owen): Just to set expectations, Private falls into a longer procurement path, but technically we can support the KMS/HSM and audit log requirements. For the immediate PoC, hosted with strict retention/segmentation might also work if the customer allows.
01:18 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Ok, good to know. Deal 1 — "AtlasHealth" (public sector healthcare insur.) — they asked for SOC2 plus data residency in eu-west. ACV ~ $420k TCV, likely decision Q4. Who wants to own outreach?
01:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood AE can co-own with Neon — I can lead demo and Redwood will provide the security packet. Sophie, can Neon own initial intro to the technical buyer?
01:45 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Yes, we'll set intro. Ibrahim will be the internal technical owner.
01:53 Speaker 5 (Ibrahim): Yep, I'll be on that. For AtlasHealth we need to validate latency at 4k context and show encryption in transit + at-rest. Also they asked about on-prem options — that might be a blocker.
02:10 Speaker 3 (Owen): For latency, we can run a short benchmark. I'm thinking we test the 4k prompt, measure p95 with a mixed batch profile; I'll share a sample config that fits their ask. Regarding on-prem, Redwood Private is the path but might be heavier. We can propose a hybrid: early hosted pilot with strict retention and then Private as a later contract.
02:30 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Hybrid sounds reasonable. Could you share an estimate on cost delta for Private?
02:36 Speaker 3 (Owen): Rough sketch: Private baseline has setup and infra licensing; for an org this size, ballpark is 30-50% higher than hosted at same throughput, but variable depending on GPU choice and quantization. I'll put numbers in the note.
02:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): Okay next, Deal 2 — "Fintronics" (mid-market fintech). ACV $180k, timeline next 60 days. They care about throughput and cost per call. Neon is leading outbound.
03:05 Speaker 4 (Carlos): They want to see a side-by-side cost model vs first-principles. Also—they asked about competitors — mentioned Databricks and Scale AI.
03:15 Speaker 1 (Maya): Right, we'll add a competitive slide. For cost we can show batching and caching levers that reduce per-token cost; Owen will outline typical gains with prefix caching.
03:30 Speaker 3 (Owen): Quick note — caching could change the perf profile, so we'll recommend a short synthetic benchmark and one small production shadow test to estimate token reduction.
03:45 Speaker 2 (Sophie): How do we present that to the customer without overpromising?
03:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): We say "sample results from similar workloads" and include caveats; propose a 2-week pilot to get real numbers.
04:05 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Deal 3 — "RetailEdge" (national retail chain). Larger, cross-org stakeholders, ACV $950k, long sales cycle. They care about model quality/regression monitoring and rollout controls.
04:20 Speaker 3 (Owen): For rollout we can demo canary and A/B features in Redwood Console and show how to tie evals to prompt sets. That usually resonates with platform teams.
04:35 Speaker 5 (Ibrahim): RetailEdge legal asked about audit logs and SSO. Can you confirm SAML/SCIM support?
04:42 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we support SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning; we'll attach the SSO integration guide.
05:00 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Good. A few risk flags across pipeline: 1) Procurement cadence on the public sector deal, 2) RetailEdge procurement wants a runbook for incident response, 3) Fintronics wants tight cost SKU — need a demo showing cost controls.
05:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): Let's talk tactical next steps: Owen will produce the perf notes for AtlasHealth and Fintronics; I'll update the spreadsheet and add ownership columns; Neon to confirm who will be the customer intro owner per deal.
05:35 Speaker 3 (Owen): I'll also include a small sample of kernel/quantization suggestions — that sometimes helps buyers understand cost tradeoffs.
05:45 Speaker 4 (Carlos): On the competitive front, Databricks is pitching a unified data and model story; Neon wants the Redwood differentiation on "production-first" and predictable economics.
06:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll craft a co-branded slide: focus on predictable latency, unit cost controls (batching/caching), and flexible deployment modes.
06:10 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Also want to ask about co-sell motions — do we have a template for partner-led deal registration or credit splits?
06:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): We have a partner playbook — Lena, can you share the partner motion doc after?
06:25 Speaker 6 (Lena): Yep, I'll drop the playbook and a sample contract clause.
06:32 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Great. On the AtlasHealth technical ask — they want encryption in transit plus key rotation proof. Ibrahim, can you capture their security contact?
06:40 Speaker 5 (Ibrahim): Will do. I'll get the contact and pass it to Maya.
06:45 Speaker 3 (Owen): For the bench tests, small note — their 4k context with structured data might hit memory patterns; we'll include suggestions for sequence bucketing and quantized model to keep costs down.
07:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): Moving on — new opportunity Neon flagged: "LogiServe" — earlier stage, potential $120k. They want a short demo this month.
07:15 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Yup, we penciled a demo for end of month. Would Redwood run a joint demo?
07:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we can. Owen, can you lead the demo with a focus on latency and error handling?
07:26 Speaker 3 (Owen): Absolutely, happy to. I'll prepare a 20-min technical demo and bring a perf slide.
07:34 Speaker 2 (Sophie): For internal Neon operations, Ava will coordinate scheduling and follow-ups.
07:40 Speaker 7 (Ava): Thanks. I'll propose two slots and sync calendars after this call.
07:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): Cool. Quick callouts: we should prioritize AtlasHealth and RetailEdge for exec involvement; Fintronics and LogiServe as fast pilots.
08:00 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Agreed. On legal/procurement: do we have a standard security questionnaire template?
08:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, OW — we'll attach a standard security packet and the SOC2 report. Lena will include the privacy whitepaper.
08:14 Speaker 6 (Lena): I'll attach both docs to the spreadsheet.
08:20 Speaker 3 (Owen): Also, a note about benchmarks — our numbers sometimes get misread when customers compare different model sizes; we'll include clarifying notes about sequence length and tokenization.
08:35 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. Let's run a quick prioritization vote — Sophie/Carlos: top 3?
08:42 Speaker 2 (Sophie): AtlasHealth, RetailEdge, Fintronics.
08:45 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Same.
08:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): Consensus. OK next, who will lead each?
08:52 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Neon will lead AtlasHealth intro to the buyer; Redwood will support demo and security packet.
08:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): For RetailEdge, Redwood will lead the initial technical demo with Neon co-selling.
09:05 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Fintronics — Neon will lead pilot negotiation; Redwood will provide cost model and perf notes.
09:12 Speaker 3 (Owen): I'll send the perf config and a short README on how we ran the benchmarks.
09:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): Good. Any blockers we haven't covered?
09:24 Speaker 5 (Ibrahim): One small thing — RetailEdge asked about model rollback policies in case of drift. Can you demo automated rollback or require manual control?
09:33 Speaker 3 (Owen): We support canary-based automatic fallback and manual rollbacks. We'll prepare a short diagram for the next call.
09:44 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Perfect. Also please include a sample evaluation rubric for quality regression detection.
09:50 Speaker 3 (Owen): Will do — tie it to prompt sets and thresholds.
09:56 Speaker 1 (Maya): Let's capture explicit next steps — Maya will update spreadsheet with owners and attach deck; Owen will send perf notes and benchmark config; Lena will attach partner playbook and security docs; Neon team to confirm internal owners for each prioritized deal.
10:12 Speaker 2 (Sophie): We'll aim to have owners confirmed by Monday.
10:16 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. Any quick Qs?
10:19 Speaker 4 (Carlos): One — pricing: do you have partner discount guidance?
10:23 Speaker 6 (Lena): We have a partner pricing policy; I'll include a note but final discounts go via contract review.
10:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): Okay, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the spreadsheet and links.
10:35 Speaker 2 (Sophie): Thanks all.
10:36 Speaker 3 (Owen): Thanks.
10:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): Bye.
